independent_prior_result.decision: LM is below both original10% goals. Retain every sample, including public token512 p95+3.7551366648520768% and all positive p50 changes; do not replay or combine percentages.

motivation: The existing ASCII fast path requires every post-normalization character to be ASCII. An ordinary English string containing Unicode punctuation can therefore still enter the Python RUNS/finditer/CJK/split/extend loop even when every lexical character is an ASCII letter or digit. A whole-current-string lexical certificate may prove that the already existing ASCII_RUNS path returns the exact same ordered tokens. No corpus text or new sample was inspected to pick this certificate and no numeric improvement is claimed.

allowed.certificate_location: The current whole string after the unchanged NFKC/CamelCase/casefold/NFKD/Mn pipeline, immediately after the unchanged existing text.isascii() fast-return branch.
allowed.eligibility: Require exact native str, exact bool query and original compiled ASCII_RUNS, RUNS, CJK_RUN, IDENTIFIER_SEPARATOR and ZH_QUESTION object identities. Then require no certificate-pattern match. Keep every unsupported case on the complete existing lexical loop. For query=True also require STOP is the captured original immutable STOP frozenset; query=False does not evaluate STOP and need not require this identity.
allowed.new_branch: Reuse ASCII_RUNS.findall(text) and the same ordered STOP filter as the existing ASCII branch. Do not normalize, rewrite source text or change token ordering/deduplication.
allowed.identity_capture: Capture the five original compiled-pattern references and original immutable string-only STOP frozenset once at module initialization. No new dependency, cache or public API.
allowed.inverse: Removing exactly the new module-level certificate/reference block and the new guarded branch must recover the entire frozen LM text.py byte-for-byte.

proof_obligations: Explicitly reject every scalar in the complete old CJK ranges, including unassigned or non-word points that the old CJK regex still recognizes. A Unicode-word-only guard is insufficient.

Reject every other Unicode word character outside lowercase ASCII letters, digits and underscore, plus any ASCII uppercase that survives an unusual prefix. All remaining non-ASCII characters are old-grammar separators.

Under the five original compiled patterns, old non-CJK matches contain only ASCII alphanumeric pieces with allowed ASCII identifier connectors; splitting those connectors gives exactly the same ordered nonempty ASCII_RUNS pieces. Prefix, suffix, repeated or mixed connectors and every separator boundary must agree.

ZH_QUESTION cannot match without a character in the excluded CJK ranges. ZH_STOP is unreachable on the eligible lexical path. For query=True specialize only with the original immutable STOP identity; all custom or replaced STOP objects use the complete old loop because membership can change later pattern hooks. Query=False performs no STOP membership.

Keep type(query) is bool so custom query truth values retain every original truth evaluation. Guard the post-normalization current text, not a pre-fold or per-word fragment. Preserve the original complete ASCII branch without additional conditions.

Use actual C-call and Python-loop-entry evidence to demonstrate eligible non-ASCII punctuation strings use the existing whole-string ASCII finder and never the old per-word loop. This is mechanism evidence only, never a timing claim.
